summary: Rate hike expectations eased this week after the soft June payrolls print, with the probability of a July FOMC hike falling to 20% from 30% — keeping equities bid and VIX contained while pressuring gold and real rates. Separately, the US refused to extend the USMCA by its July 1 deadline, with the Section 122 blanket 10% tariff now set to expire July 24, leaving North American trade policy in limbo and corporate supply chain risk elevated.
tweet: Fading Fed hike odds after weak jobs data are lifting stocks and suppressing VIX, but USMCA non-renewal and the Section 122 tariff cliff on July 24 keep trade risk squarely on the table.
